goal: Remove the duplicate GitHub Actions check-run name `check` before strict required-status-check mode is activated, by giving the workflow_dispatch-only iOS signing diagnostic its own job identity, and pin the resulting uniqueness structurally so the collision cannot return.
non_goals: Renaming the canonical CI job `check`, or any job in ci.yml, e2e.yml or native.yml
Changing the three required contexts check, playwright and native-gate
Mutating ruleset 21654011, branch protection, or any repository setting
Changing integration-protocol semantics, the integration gate, or the reviewer protocol
Renaming other duplicated job ids that are not required contexts
Changing the iOS signing diagnostic's triggers, permissions, secrets, steps or behaviour
Any hook, runtime path or tool enforcement, or production_effect enforcement
Pinning GitHub Actions to commit SHAs, or any other opportunistic workflow cleanup
acceptance_criteria: The iOS signing diagnostic's job no longer produces a check run named `check`; its job identity is unique across every workflow in the repository
The canonical required job `check` remains defined in .github/workflows/ci.yml and is unchanged
The required contexts remain exactly check, playwright and native-gate, each defined by exactly one workflow job
The iOS signing diagnostic remains workflow_dispatch-only, and its steps, environment, secrets and the script it runs are unchanged apart from the job identity

A structural spec proves each required context is produced by exactly one job across all workflows, computing the effective check-run name as the job's name override where present and the job id otherwise, so a future job named `check` cannot reintroduce the collision by either route
The required-context list the spec checks is derived from the integration protocol's REQUIRED_CHECKS rather than restated, so the two cannot drift
stop_conditions: The rename turns out to be insufficient to remove the required-check ambiguity — report before changing integration-protocol semantics, which are outside allowed_paths
Something outside this workflow depends on the job id `check` in ios-signing-check.yml — report rather than widening the change
Removing the collision would require touching ci.yml, e2e.yml, native.yml or the ruleset — stop and report
The work turns out not to fit workflow-authority / r3 / none — report before implementing
notes: Follows the integration identity gate (PR #230). Its fourth fresh-context review found that .github/workflows/ios-signing-check.yml defines a job id `check`, colliding with the canonical required context from .github/workflows/ci.yml — and both are produced by the same GitHub Actions App (integration_id 15368), so App-identity validation cannot disambiguate them. GitHub identifies a required check by context name plus integration identity, not by the workflow file that produced it, so a manual dispatch of the diagnostic can create a second `check` run. The integration gate fails closed on that ambiguity, which is correct, but the collision should be removed before strict required-status-check mode is activated. Reconnaissance: build, run and sync are also duplicated job ids, but none of them is a required context, so they are deliberately left alone. Classification: workflow-authority because this is CI/control-plane identity; r3 because .github/workflows/** is CI/workflow authority; production_effect none because the workflow is dispatch-only, touches no learner-facing code, and merging deploys nothing.
